notes: Seven distinct editorial subjects. Source articles were reviewed externally; independent corroboration of all material claims is not complete. No audio or publishing authorized.

selected_stories.title: Anthropic CEO pledges to pace AI development after Nasdaq debut
selected_stories.summary: At Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, CEO Dario Amodei said the company would slow training or deployment when needed to assess safety and keep AI under human control.
selected_stories.editorial_impact: The pledge puts AI safety commitments under the spotlight as investors evaluate the newly public company.
selected_stories.narration_text: Anthropic's chief executive says AI development must not outrun safety. At the company's Nasdaq debut, Dario Amodei pledged to pace training and deployment, even under commercial pressure.

selected_stories.title: Amazon uses shopping app to oppose NYC delivery bill
selected_stories.summary: Amazon placed messages on its website and app opposing a proposed New York City delivery law. The bill would require certain delivery contractors to become direct employees.
selected_stories.editorial_impact: The dispute raises questions about delivery labor rules and the use of major shopping platforms for lobbying.
selected_stories.narration_text: Amazon is bringing a political dispute directly to shoppers. Its website and app now urge customers to oppose a New York City delivery bill that could change how delivery workers are employed.

selected_stories.title: Bitcoin drops as technology shares face selling pressure
selected_stories.summary: CoinDesk reported bitcoin near 61,300 dollars late Thursday, with technology stocks also under pressure following Anthropic's market debut.
selected_stories.editorial_impact: The decline highlights bitcoin's exposure to risk appetite and leveraged trading rather than reliable short-term safe-haven behavior.
selected_stories.narration_text: In crypto, bitcoin slid toward sixty-one thousand three hundred dollars as technology shares weakened. The sell-off underscores how quickly digital assets can move with broader risk sentiment.

selected_stories.title: Google adds computer-use features to Gemini for Mac
selected_stories.summary: Google announced that Gemini for macOS can navigate native apps and websites to perform tasks. The initial release is limited to English-speaking subscribers in the United States.
selected_stories.editorial_impact: AI assistants are moving from answering questions toward taking actions across desktop software.
selected_stories.narration_text: Google is bringing computer control to Gemini on the Mac. The assistant can navigate apps and websites to complete tasks, with user controls to pause or approve actions.

selected_stories.title: Meta employees report possible privacy leaks in Muse AI agent
selected_stories.summary: TechCrunch, citing Reuters, reported employee concerns that test versions of Meta's Muse assistant surfaced information belonging to other accounts. Meta said employee builds differ from public versions.
selected_stories.editorial_impact: The reported incidents underline privacy risks in assistants that access personal data across services.
selected_stories.narration_text: But more capable assistants also create privacy risks. Meta employees reportedly saw its Muse agent surface information from other accounts. Meta says employee test versions differ from the public app.

selected_stories.title: Superhuman expands its Go AI assistant across workplace tools
selected_stories.summary: Superhuman announced a more personalized Go assistant, agents in Docs, and integrations with third-party services.
selected_stories.editorial_impact: The launch reflects growing competition to make AI agents part of everyday workplace workflows.
selected_stories.narration_text: Meanwhile, Superhuman is expanding its Go assistant across documents, email, and connected workplace tools. The race is shifting toward agents that can coordinate work across applications.

selected_stories.title: Everful raises $48.5 million for AI-enabled factory sourcing
selected_stories.summary: Everful announced a 48.5 million dollar Series A to expand its platform connecting smaller retailers with Chinese factories and managing sourcing and logistics.
selected_stories.editorial_impact: The funding shows continued investment in technology that reshapes cross-border commerce and supply chains.
selected_stories.narration_text: And in startup funding, Everful raised forty-eight point five million dollars to connect retailers with Chinese factories. The platform combines sourcing, logistics, and software in a competitive global trade market.
